summary: CPU research: how to best combine SuffixDecoding (model-free) + MTP drafts + a lossless tree verifier to BEAT native E5 at B=1, given the leg-sweep finding that swapping MTP spine for suffix loses (sub-native ~2.94). Survey online frontier (hybrid/multi-source spec decoding, optimal tree shape), mine our own git history (FR13 was originally MTP ⊕ suffix-fusion), and synthesize concrete rankable designs (add-not-swap, adaptive grafting, hybrid fallback). NO GPU, NO implementation - designs to bring to the user.

survey.hybridSources:
SOTA model-free + model-based hybrid drafters, with MECHANISM + reported gains:

1) SuffixDecoding (NeurIPS-2025 spotlight, arXiv 2411.04975; Apache-2.0; vLLM `speculative_config={"method":"suffix"}` via arctic-inference) — MODEL-FREE. Drafts from a suffix-tree lookup (per-request tree over prompt+generated, PLUS a GLOBAL tree over prior request outputs). MatchPattern on the last p tokens -> greedy best-first expansion into a speculation TREE scored by empirical path-frequency D(N); adaptive length MAX_SPEC = alpha*p. Reported: SWE-Bench end-to-end 1.8-4.5x over vanilla; AgenticSQL 5.3x over vanilla / 2.8x over EAGLE-2/3 / 1.9x over Token Recycling. Wins on code/agentic/verbatim-echo, LOSES to EAGLE on novel prose (Spec-Bench ~1.6-1.8) — that loss is why its headline mode is a hybrid fallback.
   - TAU-GATED FALLBACK (the exact mechanism): every step, FIRST speculate with SuffixDecoding; compute SCORE(T_spec) = the path-frequency-weighted score of the proposed suffix tree. If SCORE(T_spec) > tau, USE the suffix draft; ELSE FALL BACK to the model-based drafter (EAGLE-3). It is a PER-STEP PICK-ONE switch (not a merge). Practical tau: set tau ~ the mean-accepted-tokens (MAT) of the fallback model. With EAGLE-3 (MAT~=4.65), tau~=5-7 gives 2.5x on Spec-Bench mixed workloads; tau=0 (suffix-only) is optimal for highly-repetitive agentic tasks.

2) Hybrid Verified Decoding (arXiv 2606.01019) — the LEARNED upgrade of the tau gate, directly on point for our per-row tax. Instead of a fixed tau on a frequency score, it trains a lightweight MLP to PREDICT the accepted-length of the cache/suffix draft from PRE-verification features (suffix score, decode position, recent history, draft structure). If predicted accepted-length >= tau (they use 6), verify the cache draft; else fall back to EAGLE-3. Predictor trained by REPLAY-supervision (replay cache lookups on recorded target traces, label with actual accepted-length, squared-error regression — no extra inference). Gains: 2.97x vs greedy, 2.64x vs SuffixDecoding, 2.73x avg vs EAGLE-3 on agentic. Key allocation insight: high-payoff cache drafts (accepted-len>=6) are only 4.8-8.9% of states; predictor hits 78-88% precision at finding them -> verify selectively, skip wasted overhead.

3) REST (NAACL-2024, arXiv 2311.08252; FasterDecoding/REST) — model-free retrieval. Suffix-ARRAY over a datastore for fast CPU exact-match; retrieve continuations, build a Trie, prune low-weight branches, verify the subtree with tree-attention. No training; instantly attaches to any model.

4) Token Recycling (ACL-2025, arXiv 2408.08696) — model-free, train-free. Stores top-k candidate next-tokens per token in a vocab-sized adjacency matrix (hot-start inherited across queries), BFS-builds a draft tree, tree-attention verify, then updates the matrix. ~2x speedup; ~30% over prior train-free.

5) Lookahead Decoding (ICML-2024, arXiv 2402.02057) — model-free, EXACT. Jacobi iteration generates n-grams in a 2D window; an n-gram POOL caches trajectory n-grams; a verification branch string-matches pool n-grams whose first token == last input token and verifies them in the same forward (distribution-preserving). 1.5-2.3x.

6) Ouroboros (EMNLP-2024, arXiv 2402.13720) — combines a small draft MODEL with a phrase candidate POOL (model-free), reusing successful phrases across iterations to make longer drafts; up to 2.8x, no training.

7) PLD / prompt-lookup — degenerate model-free n-gram-from-prompt; the trivial baseline our suffix global-tree subsumes.

Pattern across all: model-free sources are CHEAP (CPU, no draft forward) and win on echo/repetition (code/agentic); model-based (EAGLE/MTP) win on novel continuation. The frontier merges them — either pick-one-per-step (tau gate) or graft-into-one-tree (Graft, below).
survey.optimalTreeShape:
SEQUOIA (ICML-2024, arXiv 2402.12374; infini-ai-lab) is the DP-optimal tree builder and the directly-relevant cost-model lever for our per-node tax:

- NODE SCORE: for node v with root-path child-index list Path(v), f(v) = product over i in Path(v) of p_i, where p_i is the acceptance prob at the i-th child position. EXPECTED GENERATED TOKENS of a tree T (Prop 3.4): F(T) = sum over v in T of f(v) (each node's accept-probability-weighted contribution).
- DP RECURRENCE (maximize expected tokens for a size-n tree): table T[n,b] = max expected tokens for a tree of size n whose root has b direct children. Base T[1,0]=1. Recurrence: T[n,b] = max over m in [1,n-1] of { T[n-m, b-1] + P[b] * T_max[m] }, where T_max[m] = max over j in [0,B] of T[m,j]. Reading: add a b-th child subtree of size m only if its marginal P[b]*T_max[m] beats spending those m nodes on the earlier branches. This is exactly the marginal "does this extra node pay for itself" test we need per verify-row.
- HARDWARE-AWARE OPTIMIZER (the cost-model principle): with empirically measured G(n,d) (expected tokens at size n, depth d) and t(n) (hardware time to verify n tokens, normalized) and draft/verify ratio c, pick (n,d) to MAXIMIZE Speedup(n,d) = G(n,d) / (t(n) + d*c). It auto-selects tree SIZE and DEPTH from the device's own latency curve t(n). Principle: on cheap-verify hardware t(n) is nearly flat in n -> grow wide/big; where each node costs real time (OUR regime: each verify row = one lm-head GEMV + GDN state traffic, t(n) STEEP in n) -> the optimal tree is SMALL and the DP stops adding nodes early — you add a node only while its marginal P[b]*T_max[m] exceeds dt/dn. DEPTH is bought sequentially (d*c term) so depth has a separate marginal price.
- ROBUST VERIFICATION: sampling-WITHOUT-replacement (track rejected set S, never re-propose; fall back to uniform over un-rejected vocab when high-prob drafts exhausted). Theorem 3.7: satisfies BOTH the optimal-transport (high-temp) and cover (low-temp) properties -> robust across temperatures, unlike SpecInfer/top-k. This is target-distribution-preserving = lossless, same class as our drafter-agnostic per-path rejection (SpecInfer Def 4.1 / STree).

SpecInfer (arXiv 2305.09781) is the foundational token-tree verifier (tree-attention + per-path rejection, Thm 4.2 MSS proves multi-candidate losslessness) — the theorem our committer rests on.

Tree-shape-vs-accept literature consensus: under a per-node cost, expected-accepts is CONCAVE in tree size and the optimum is interior — beyond a point each added node's marginal accept < its cost. Depth and width have DIFFERENT prices (depth = sequential drafter forwards; width = parallel verify rows). This maps exactly onto our asymmetric cost: MTP DEPTH costs head forwards, WIDTH/SUFFIX growth is free draft (verify rows only).
survey.multiSourceMerge:
Two distinct ways the frontier shares ONE tree between a model-based and a model-free source:

A) PICK-ONE-PER-STEP (no shared tree): SuffixDecoding's tau gate and Not-a-Bandit. Not-a-Bandit (arXiv 2510.20064) frames multi-drafter choice as an ONLINE no-regret learning problem (NOT a bandit — it observes every drafter's would-be reward each step via the verify result, so it's full-information prediction-with-experts, achieving sublinear regret vs the best single drafter in hindsight). It SELECTS one drafter per step, does not fuse. Cheap, but throws away the non-selected source's tokens.

B) GRAFT-INTO-ONE-TREE (the directly-relevant SOTA): "Draft Less, Retrieve More: Hybrid Tree Construction for Speculative Decoding" / Graft (arXiv 2605.20104). MECHANISM = prune-then-graft: (1) PRUNE — confidence-based dynamic-depth pruning cuts low-confidence autoregressive (model-based, EAGLE-3) draft branches at calibrated depth checkpoints; (2) GRAFT — retrieved (model-free) candidates fill the topological gaps the pruning opened; (3) flatten BOTH retained-draft + grafted-retrieval nodes into ONE hybrid tree T_s = T_s^draft UNION G_s^ret with |T_s| = K_max (verification budget preserved, single target pass). NODE-BUDGET ALLOCATION PRINCIPLE (the key rule): budget is allocated DYNAMICALLY by pruning depth, not fixed upfront — "shallower pruning stages allocate fewer draft nodes and grant a larger budget to retrieval." Concretely (K_max=60): shallow prune d0 -> keep 8 draft / 52 retrieval; intermediate d1 -> 24 draft / 36 retrieval; deep d5 -> 40 draft / 20 retrieval; no-prune -> base tree, ~0 retrieval. COVERAGE: retrieval is ROOT-CENTERED (fills the gaps near where the model-based drafter became uncertain), model-based keeps the high-confidence branches. GAINS: vs EAGLE-3 (model-only) 7.4-21.8% (short-ctx) / 10.3-20.2% (long-ctx) faster, +3.2-8.5% MAT; vs ECHO (pruning-only) 2.9-8.9% faster and +4.0-8.3% MAT. Conclusion: pruning and retrieval are COMPLEMENTARY — the hybrid beats either alone.

The governing principle across A and B: spend nodes on the source with the higher EXPECTED marginal accept AT THAT TREE POSITION. Model-based wins where the model is confident (high-confidence shallow spine); model-free/retrieval wins where the model is uncertain OR where echo/repetition makes a long verbatim continuation cheap (deep tail, gaps). Graft turns the model's OWN confidence into the allocation signal — graft retrieval exactly where the learned drafter degrades.
survey.bestIdeasForUs:
Mapped to our regime (Qwen3.6-27b-fp8, B=1, memory-bandwidth-bound, n_pad<=16, drafter-agnostic LOSSLESS verifier already built; MTP depth costs head-forwards, suffix/width is free draft; ADD-NOT-SWAP after the leg-sweep finding that swap-based legs reach only A/E~2.94 < native 3.16):

1) ADOPT THE GRAFT CONFIDENCE-GATED ALLOCATION, NOT A SWAP (Graft 2605.20104 + our own leg-sweep). Our leg-sweep already proved fixed-position legs and spine-shortening swaps lose. Graft's lesson is the fix: keep the FULL MTP spine (don't forfeit the reliable deep accepts d3 0.483/d4 0.379), and graft free suffix nodes ONLY where the MTP head is UNCERTAIN (low top-1 margin) — i.e. at the largest reject bucket. Our own data names that bucket: 62% of reject-steps land at STEP-0, which currently has NO branch (root top-2 is dead code). A root-sibling + suffix graft at step-0 is the single highest-EV add (Graft: "retrieval is root-centered, where the drafter is uncertain").

2) ADD A SUFFIX TAIL BEYOND THE MTP TIP (not swapping d3-d5). Our CPU hit-rate gate already measured the suffix tail at A=2.32 expected accepts (global-warm), bimodal (69.9% reach the 3-cap). Because suffix/width is FREE draft and our verifier is lossless for any tree, EXTENDING the spine past the MTP-5 tip with a suffix chain (within the 16-node budget) adds net-new accept opportunity at only +verify-row cost — the genuine native-beating lever the swap framing missed.

3) USE SEQUOIA'S DP WITH OUR REAL t(n), DON'T HAND-PICK THE SHAPE. Plug our measured per-row tax into Speedup(n,d)=G(n,d)/(t(n)+d*c) and run the T[n,b] DP. Crucially t(n) for us is NOT flat: each row is an lm-head GEMV AND, on the legacy route, +2.9 ms/node GDN state traffic — so the DP will correctly stop early and prefer SHALLOW+WIDE-at-root (matches our tree-reshape unifying-lever memory). Note: the +2.9 ms/node tax is exactly what the FR13 replay route removes (0.86x native); once replay lands, t(n) flattens and the DP will license a BIGGER suffix tail — sequence the two.

4) USE A LEARNED/CHEAP GATE TO ALLOCATE THE TAIL (Hybrid Verified Decoding 2606.01019 + the tau gate). We already have the perfect signal sources for free: MTP top-1 margin (model-based confidence) and suffix match-length / path-frequency D(N) (model-free confidence). Gate: graft the suffix tail ONLY when suffix predicted-accept-length is high AND/OR MTP margin is low — exactly the ADAPTIVE direction the prompt asked for. Replay-supervision (label banked SWE streams with actual accepted-length, regress on pre-verify features) is CPU-only and directly reuses our banked traces — buildable now, no GPU.

5) GLOBAL SUFFIX TREE IS A HARD PRECONDITION. Both SuffixDecoding and our CPU gate agree: the win rides on the GLOBAL cross-request tree (shared agentic boilerplate); per-request short streams contribute ~nothing, cold = thin +0.82 margin. Warm the global tree from prior SWE outputs before any GPU arm.

6) KEEP THE LOSSLESS GUARANTEE — no reward-hack risk. Every grafted suffix/MTP node is just a descriptor candidate; a miss is rejected (costs a row, never a wrong commit) under our per-path SpecInfer/STree rejection. Sequoia's sampling-without-replacement (Thm 3.7) is an OPTIONAL temp-robustness upgrade to our verifier, same lossless class. None of these add a lossy mechanism (no copy/dense/splice/multispine).

CAVEAT to bind: suffix tails sit at the SAME deep rows as our open cat9 ~4.6% argmax-flip defect, so any suffix arm is DOWNSTREAM of the cat9 lossless chase and must re-gate on the per-token argmax-vs-clean-oracle probe, never scalar accept/event (scalar metrics are blind to small-rate per-token defects).

survey.mtpDrafters:
HOW MTP HEADS DRAFT MULTI-DEPTH + PER-DEPTH DECAY:

DeepSeek-V3 MTP (arXiv 2412.19437) is the canonical sequential/cascaded MTP: D lightweight single-transformer-layer heads, each conditioned on the PREVIOUS head's hidden state, so depth costs sequential head forwards (a depth-d draft = d sequential passes — this is exactly our "MTP DEPTH = head forwards" cost axis). Shipped V3 uses D=2 (predict the +1 token natively, +1 extra via the head). Per-depth accept: the SECOND-token head accepts 80-90% across topics → 1.8x TPS (tech report §, and arXiv 2505.09343 "Insights into DeepSeek-V3" gives the 80-90%/1.8x figures explicitly). The architecture (sequential, full causal chain, single-layer heads) is the one "widely integrated into MiMo, GLM, LongCat, and Qwen3-Next" (arXiv 2603.23911) — i.e. OUR Qwen3-Next MTP is a DeepSeek-V3-lineage cascaded MTP.

PER-DEPTH DECAY IS STEEP AND IS THE CORE CONSTRAINT: the published pattern (DeepSeek ~85% at d2) plus our own measured cat9 caterpillar (FR13_SUFFIX_MTP_HYBRID_DESIGN.md / FR13_DIRECTION_AND_NUMBERS.md) — d0 0.87, d1 0.83, d3 0.483, d4 0.379, d5 0.30 — confirm a confidence cliff: MTP is RELIABLE shallow (d0-d2 ~0.83-0.87) and DECAYS fast by d3-d5. This is the literature-consistent "confident-shallow" profile. MTP WIDTH (top-k alts per depth) and the deeper tail are where the head is least reliable, which is precisely where a free/cheap deep source should take over. Sequential-MTP per-depth decay is the EXACT signal that motivates confidence-gated allocation (next column): the head itself emits the per-depth distribution that says where to stop trusting it.

KEY NUMBER FOR US: our MTP spine reaches native E5 3.16 accept/event over 5 depths; the per-depth product (0.87*0.83*...) is what generates that. ADD-not-SWAP must preserve the reliable d0-d2 mass — the leg-sweep finding confirmed swapping deep MTP rows for suffix forfeits the d3-d4 0.483/0.379 reliable-deep accepts and drops to A/E 2.94 < native.
survey.treeDrafters:
TREE-PICK MECHANISMS (all share one principle: rank by PATH-PRODUCT-OF-CONFIDENCES = global accept-prob estimate; this is what our drafter-agnostic verifier consumes as candidate-tree priority):

MEDUSA (arXiv 2401.10774): K parallel heads (head i predicts depth i), each top-s candidates, combined into a FIXED Cartesian-product tree with tree attention (ancestor-only mask + position indices). No per-step adaptivity — tree is static, picked offline by accuracy. Typical-acceptance scheme (not exact); 2.2-3.6x. Relevant as the "parallel-head → tree" template, but its FIXED tree is the thing EAGLE-2/OPT-Tree/Sequoia improve on.

EAGLE-2 (arXiv 2406.16858, EMNLP 2024): DYNAMIC tree in two phases. EXPANSION: value V_i = product of draft-model confidences along root→i path = estimated GLOBAL acceptance probability; expand the top-k highest-V frontier nodes one layer via one tree-attention forward. RERANK: keep the top-m nodes by V_i (ties favor shallower), flatten for verification. Draft model is WELL-CALIBRATED so confidence ≈ accept-rate. 3.05-4.26x. THIS IS THE DIRECTLY-APPLICABLE MECHANISM: V_i (path-product) is exactly the priority our candidate-tree descriptor should carry to decide which of the 16 nodes to spend on.

EAGLE-3 (arXiv 2503.01840, NeurIPS 2025): drops feature-prediction for direct token prediction + multi-layer (low/mid/high) feature fusion via "training-time test" → scales with data, up to 6.5x (1.4x over EAGLE-2). MAT (mean accepted tokens) ≈ 4.65 — this is the τ-anchor used by SuffixDecoding's hybrid (see confidenceAllocation).

SEQUOIA (arXiv 2402.12374): OFFLINE dynamic-programming optimizer that finds the tree TOPOLOGY maximizing expected accepted tokens at each node budget, and a HARDWARE-AWARE optimizer that picks tree size/depth for the platform — pre-computes child-size splits, regenerates topology once at runtime. Directly relevant to our GB10 cost model: it formalizes "for THIS hardware's per-row tax, what tree shape maximizes accept/cost" — our verify-row tax (one lm-head GEMV/node) + GDN per-node state tax is exactly a Sequoia hardware input.

OPT-Tree (arXiv 2406.17276): per-step greedy tree maximizing E(acceptance length) under node budget n; node prob p̂ = product of path probabilities; stop expanding when marginal gain < drafting overhead δ (δ ∈ [μ,1], μ = draft-time/decode-time). Confirms the adaptive-shape law (see confidenceAllocation) and validates E(A)/path-product as a reliable accept proxy (numbers: ~3.9-7.7 mean accept-len at 25-60 nodes).
survey.confidenceAllocation:
YES — there is a clear, convergent, literature result on confidence/entropy-gated tree allocation, and it maps almost 1:1 onto our MTP(confident-shallow) vs suffix(cheap-deep) question:

THE ADAPTIVE-SHAPE LAW (SAGE arXiv 2602.00523; OPT-Tree 2406.17276; HeteroSpec 2505.13254; SAGE summary explicit): use the draft distribution's normalized ENTROPY as a confidence signal, then — LOW entropy / HIGH confidence → DEEPER-and-NARROWER tree (push speculation depth, the model knows what comes next); HIGH entropy / LOW confidence → SHALLOWER-and-WIDER tree (diversify across alternatives, don't waste depth on branches that'll be rejected). SAGE: 3.18-3.36x lossless on VLMs. OPT-Tree gives the same law from the E(A)-maximization math (deeper-fewer-children when draft-target aligned, broader-shallower when not).

HETEROSPEC (2505.13254) is the most operational: a "cumulative Meta-Path Top-K entropy" metric measures how easy/hard the current path is; an OFFLINE-TRAINED CART regression tree maps that entropy to discrete BINS that schedule DRAFT DEPTH and PRUNE WIDTH per position. Result: 4.26x e2e, +6% acceptance length, 5-20% FEWER verification calls vs fixed stop-criteria, no draft-model retraining, beats EAGLE-3. The "fewer verification calls" is the row-tax win we care about on GB10.

THE EXPLICIT TWO-SOURCE GATE (SuffixDecoding hybrid, arXiv 2411.04975 / suffix-decoding.github.io): THIS IS THE LITERAL "allocate between confident-shallow (model) and cheap-deep (model-free) source" result. Rule: speculate with the FASTER model-free SuffixDecoding WHENEVER its speculation SCORE (driven by suffix pattern-MATCH LENGTH) is high enough; FALL BACK to the model-based drafter (EAGLE-3) when the score is too low. Confidence gate = pattern match length; longer match → more accepted tokens (their left chart) and deeper adaptive tree (MAX_SPEC = α·p, p = match length). Threshold τ ≈ mean-accepted-tokens of the fallback (EAGLE-3 MAT≈4.65 → τ=5-7) → 2.5x on Spec-Bench mixed, 5.3x AgenticSQL. So: gate on SUFFIX MATCH-LENGTH (cheap-deep source's own confidence), use model where suffix is cold/uncertain.

ONLINE/NO-REGRET SELECTION (Not-a-Bandit arXiv 2510.20064): hedging/exponential-weights over heterogeneous drafters, weighted by runtime acceptance rates, provably no-regret vs best fixed drafter — a principled way to learn the MTP-vs-suffix mix online if a static gate is too blunt.

NET: the field says (a) use entropy/path-product as confidence, (b) deeper-narrower when confident else shallower-wider, (c) for a model + model-free pair gate on the model-free source's MATCH-LENGTH confidence with τ≈fallback-MAT, (d) optionally learn the mix online.
survey.bestIdeasForUs:
Ranked, all ADD-NOT-SWAP / ADAPTIVE (per the leg-sweep finding that swap-based legs lose to tip, and respecting the no-reward-hack ban — every node below is just a candidate in our drafter-agnostic descriptor, lossless by per-path rejection):

1. SUFFIX-MATCH-LENGTH GATE (the single strongest, directly from SuffixDecoding hybrid). Keep the FULL MTP spine d0-d4 (don't shorten it — preserves the reliable 0.483/0.379 deep accepts). EXTEND beyond the MTP tip with a free suffix chain ONLY WHEN the current suffix match-length p exceeds a threshold (τ analog). When suffix is cold/short-match (cold-start, novel prose), spend those 16-budget nodes on MTP WIDTH (top-2 legs at the confident-shallow depths) instead. This is exactly the hybrid τ≈fallback-MAT rule, with MTP as fallback and suffix as the cheap-deep extension. Our CPU gate already showed E[suffix accept at tip]=2.32 with global warm — gate it on p so the cold +0.82 worst case never fires when MTP width would do better.

2. ENTROPY-GATED ADD: use the MTP head's OWN per-depth distribution (it emits it for free) as the SAGE/HeteroSpec entropy signal. Where MTP is CONFIDENT (low-entropy d0-d2, 0.83-0.87) → keep the spine narrow+deep, NO width spend (width is wasted, top-1 will be accepted). Where MTP gets UNCERTAIN (d3+ entropy rising, accept 0.483→0.30) → that is where to ADD: either a top-2 MTP leg (width, free draft) OR graft the suffix tail. This makes width/suffix grafting ADAPTIVE to MTP uncertainty rather than uniform — directly the HeteroSpec "allocate budget to where it pays" result. Note our own finding: 62% of rejects land at STEP-0 with no branch rescue (depth-1-sibling gap) — entropy at d0 is the cheapest, highest-ROI place to add the missing sibling.

3. PATH-PRODUCT PRIORITY ON THE DESCRIPTOR (EAGLE-2/OPT-Tree). Carry V_i = product-of-confidences along each candidate's path in the descriptor and fill the n_pad≤16 budget by top-V_i, NOT by a fixed shape. This is free to compute (MTP gives per-depth probs; suffix gives empirical freq C(N)) and is the proven way to pick which 16 nodes maximize accept/event. Lets MTP-near-nodes and suffix-deep-nodes compete on one currency (estimated global accept prob) so the budget self-allocates.

4. HARDWARE-AWARE SHAPE (Sequoia). Our binding tax is per-node GDN state traffic (~2.9 ms/node replay) + one lm-head GEMV/node, B=1 memory-bandwidth-bound. Run a Sequoia-style DP offline that maximizes E(accepted)/E(cost) where cost = (verify rows)×(GEMV) + (GDN nodes)×(state tax), using our measured per-depth accepts. Because MTP-WIDTH and SUFFIX nodes are FREE drafts (only add verify rows, the cheap axis) while MTP-DEPTH costs head forwards, the DP will naturally favor wide+suffix-deep over more MTP depth — quantifying the ADD-not-deepen intuition.

5. ONLINE MIX (Not-a-Bandit) as a v2: if a static match-length τ is too blunt across SWE task phases, learn the MTP-width-vs-suffix-graft weighting online by runtime acceptance (no-regret). Low priority — start with the static match-length gate.

THE HONEST CAVEAT (from our own evidence): exact CPU evidence has tip-grow at only A/E 2.94 < native 3.16, and the native-beating 3.43 lives entirely inside an UNMEASURED modeled d0 leg-rescue. So the winning config is almost certainly ADD-WIDTH-AT-d0 (fix the 62%-step-0-reject gap with a root sibling — our docs already flag root top-2 as dead code) PLUS suffix-extend-beyond-tip-when-match-is-long, NOT either alone. The literature predicts this exact shape (shallow-wide where uncertain = d0 sibling; deep-narrow where confident = suffix tail off the surviving tip). All downstream of the cat9 lossless chase; gate any build on the per-token argmax-vs-clean-oracle probe, never scalar accept/event.

1. THE SEAM IS LOSSLESS-CLEAN BY CONSTRUCTION (red-team holds=True): suffix tokens are descriptor candidates only; per-path SpecInfer/STree rejection on the drafter-agnostic committer. No new lossy mechanism, no copy/dense/splice/multispine = not a reward-hack. BUT the hybrid INHERITS the open cat9 committer defect: the ~4.3-4.6% deep-row non-argmax flips (the 22-flip chase) — suffix tails live at exactly those deep rows. So suffix-fusion is DOWNSTREAM of the cat9 lossless chase, never before it. Re-gate on the per-token argmax-vs-clean-oracle probe, never scalar accept/event (scalar is blind to small-rate flips — commit 30d749a4).

2. SWAP-BASED (shortening the MTP spine to fund suffix) DOES NOT BEAT NATIVE. The leg-grow n-sweep + tip-grow both top out at A/E ≈ 2.94, BELOW cat9 3.18 / native E5 3.16. Mechanism: shortening the reliable deep-MTP spine (d3 0.483 / d4 0.379) for echo-dependent suffix forfeits net accept. The +1.18-1.60 "margin" was a PORTION comparison (3-deep tail's 2.32 vs displaced d3-d5's 0.721), NOT the full-config number. So swap-based hybrids are not the native-beating route. (This is exactly the prompt's leg-sweep finding — confirmed in the banked JSON.)

3. LEGS DO NOT BEAT TIP. Suffix payoff is FLAT across graft depth (1.43-1.70); a leg's only possible edge is catching early divergences the tip misses, but under asymmetric cost (MTP depth = head forwards; suffix growth = free) the optimizer never selects a leg at any n (best-with-legs accept/cost falls 0.323→0.241 as n 2→5). The one native-beating raw 3.43 lives entirely in the MODELED, unreliable capped-d0 catch (raw 1.76 = the cat9-vs-native trajectory confound, NOT a real rank-2 recovery). VERDICT: do NOT fund the leg-grow GPU arm — the true per-depth top-k LEG drafts do not exist anywhere on CPU (fr10_mtp_draft_trace.jsonl holds only width-1 MTP-5 spine), so the decisive d0 leg-catch is GPU-only.

4. THE cat10 −0.27 "DILUTION" IS AN ACCOUNTING ARTIFACT (commit f0bf9e0e / bcb65545), NOT real dilution: trajectory confound + sibling-stop denominator + strict_mask makes the root sibling attention-invisible to the spine so it CANNOT dilute. So there was no real dilution trap to beat — the suffix margin stands on its own.

5. OPEN / UNRESOLVED: the native-beating number requires either NET-NEW accept beyond the FULL MTP spine (ADD-not-SWAP: keep full MTP, extend the tip with free suffix nodes within the 16-node budget) or CHEAPER rows (the FR13 replay route gets per-forward HBM tax to 0.86× native, decoupling verify-row cost). All numbers from banked CPU evidence: cat9 per-depth accept {d0 0.871, d1 0.828, d2 0.638, d3 0.483, d4 0.379} (output/fr13_leg_suffix/leg_suffix_results.json:9-23); cat9 measured accept/event 3.18 = spine-only E 2.359 + branch/greedy-rescue bonus 0.821; native E5 B=1 3.076 (FR13_DIRECTION_AND_NUMBERS.md:38). Suffix E[min(CORRECT_LEN,T)] is FLAT vs graft depth (leg-sweep PART1: ~1.43-1.70 cap3), deployed global-warm cap3=2.317 leaky / 1.899 strict / 0.82 cold (suffix_hitrate_results.json:30-32; leg_suffix_results.json part1). Budget n_pad<=16; MTP DEPTH=head forwards, suffix=FREE draft (verify rows only). All lossless by construction: suffix/MTP tokens are descriptor candidates only; per-path SpecInfer Def 4.1 / STree rejection (FR13_SUFFIX_MTP_HYBRID_DESIGN.md:26-34) — a miss costs a verify row, never a wrong commit. No copy/dense/splice/multispine.

=== DESIGN A — FULL-cat9 + suffix-beyond-the-tip (pure ADD-NOT-SWAP) [THE BEST BET] ===
TOPOLOGY: keep the entire 9-node cat9 caterpillar unchanged (spine d0..d4 + per-depth top-2 branch), then graft a single model-free suffix continuation CHAIN of length T onto the d4 SPINE TIP. parent extends cat9: node10=child(d4-tip), node11=child(10),...  T in {3,5}; total rows = 9+T = 12 (T=3) or 14 (T=5), <=16.
SOURCE PER NODE: nodes 0-8 = MTP (spine d0..d4 = 5 sequential head forwards; per-depth top-2 alts = free width). nodes 9..9+T = SuffixDecoding global-tree continuation off the tip (MatchPattern on last p committed tokens, freq-scored best path; arctic SuffixDecodingCache.speculate).
BUDGET: MTP head forwards = 5 (unchanged from cat9). Suffix tail adds T verify rows, ZERO head forwards. 12-14 rows.
ACCEPT INTUITION: the suffix fires only when the FULL spine survives to its tip, P(reach d4 tip)=prod(p)=0.0842. Extra = 0.0842 x E[suffix]. T=3: +0.195 leaky / +0.160 strict; T=5: +0.286 / +0.227. Layered on cat9 3.18 => 3.34-3.47 (leaky) / 3.34-3.41 (strict) — STRICTLY > native 3.076 and > cat9 3.18. The gain is SMALL because reach-tip is rare, but it is NET-NEW (no MTP spine shortened => no forfeited deep accepts — this is precisely what kills the swap arms) and FREE (suffix=verify rows only). Critically, at graft-depth g=4 the deep-spine-kept = 0 (Design4 sweep: at g<4 a graft DISPLACES deep spine = the swap regime that the leg-sweep measured tops at A/E 2.94 < native). g=4 is the ONLY non-displacing graft, so it is the only one that strictly dominates cat9.
LOSSLESS: suffix tokens are descriptor candidates on the spine path-to-root; deep grafts in-scope for per-path branch oracle (native-on-branch-path, SpecInfer Def 4.1). INHERITS the open cat9 ~4.6% deep-row argmax-flip defect (suffix tails sit at exactly those deep rows) — re-gate on the per-token argmax-vs-clean-oracle probe (fr13_gold_margin_probe), never scalar accept/event.

=== DESIGN B — DEPTH-3 spine + suffix-T tip + KEEP cat9 deep branches as cheap rescue (HYBRID-MERGE) ===
TOPOLOGY: MTP spine d0..d2 (3 head forwards) with top-2 branch at each of d0/d1/d2 (6 nodes) + suffix chain T=4 off the d2 tip (4 nodes) + a 1-2 node suffix/sibling rescue at d0 (the largest reject bucket). ~6+4+2 = 12 rows.
SOURCE: nodes = MTP spine+width (d0-d2), SuffixDecoding tip chain (T=4), SuffixDecoding short rescue at d0.
BUDGET: MTP head forwards = 3 (vs cat9's 5 — SAVES 2 head forwards = real B=1 decode-latency cut, the dominant tax per the prompt). 12 rows.
ACCEPT INTUITION: this is a SWAP (shortens spine to d2) so by the leg-sweep's exact tip-grow result it tops at A/E ~2.94 (raw 3.43 only inside MODELED leg-rescue) — BELOW native 3.16 on accept/event ALONE. BUT it trades accept for SPEED: 3 head forwards instead of 5. Under the prompt's cost model (MTP depth = sequential head forwards = real latency; suffix free), if 2 fewer head-forwards per event outweighs the ~0.24 accept/event drop in TPS terms, it can beat native on TPS even at lower accept/event. This is the speed-first lever, NOT the accept-first lever. NEEDS GPU to settle (the head-forward-vs-accept TPS tradeoff is unmeasured).
LOSSLESS: same as A; per-path rejection, drafter-agnostic.

=== DESIGN C — ADAPTIVE confidence-gated tail length (SuffixDecoding MAX_SPEC=alpha*p, our budget version) ===
TOPOLOGY: full cat9 (9 nodes) + a VARIABLE-length suffix tail beyond the tip whose length T is chosen per-step by the SuffixDecoding tree score / match-length: long tail (T up to 7, filling budget to 16) when the suffix match is long+high-frequency (echo region, uncapped CORRECT_LEN p90=22, max 51), short or zero when the match is weak. Also gate by MTP tip entropy: only spend deep suffix rows when the MTP tip is confident the spine reached it.
SOURCE: cat9 MTP (5 head fwd) + adaptive SuffixDecoding tail (0..7 rows).
BUDGET: 9 + T(adaptive 0..7) <= 16.
ACCEPT INTUITION: Design A spends a FIXED T=3-5 tail and captures cap3=2.317 of the echo. But uncapped suffix CORRECT_LEN is bimodal (69.9% reach full 3-cap, frac_ge5_uncapped=0.582, p90=22). On the high-confidence echo states the tail should be LONG (n_pad lets T=7 capture ~3.4 expected), on low-confidence states T=0 (don't waste rows). Per SuffixDecoding's own adaptive MAX_SPEC=alpha*p result and Hybrid-Verified-Decoding's learned allocation (predicted accepted-len>=6 are only 4.8-8.9% of states, predictor hits 78-88% precision), allocating the deep rows ONLY to high-payoff states raises the realized extra above Design A's flat +0.19. LOSSLESS: identical; the adaptive length only changes WHICH/HOW-MANY candidates are in the descriptor, never the rejection rule.

=== DESIGN D — SEQUOIA-optimized merged tree under the GB10 per-row + per-node-GDN cost model ===
TOPOLOGY: do not hand-fix the shape. Feed the Sequoia DP optimizer (arXiv 2402.12374) the empirical node-accept table — MTP per-depth {0.871..0.379} for spine/width nodes, suffix FLAT ~1.5 (cap3) for graft nodes — plus the GB10 cost t(n) (lm-head GEMV per row ~2.9 ms + GDN state tax per node) and node budget 16, and let T[n,b] = max_m {T[n-m,b-1] + P[b]*Tmax[m]} choose the topology (how many MTP-width children, where to place suffix sub-chains, depth vs breadth) that maximizes expected accepted tokens per hardware-time. The marginal test 'does this extra node pay for itself' is exactly our per-verify-row question.
SOURCE: optimizer-assigned mix of MTP-spine / MTP-width / suffix nodes.
BUDGET: <=16 by construction; optimizer respects MTP-depth=head-forward cost separately from suffix=free.
ACCEPT INTUITION: Designs A-C are hand-picked points; Sequoia finds the cost-model optimum over the whole 16-node space, so by construction >= the best hand-design. It will likely confirm A's structure (full spine + tip suffix) is near-optimal for accept-max, or find a better breadth/depth split. This is the principled way to settle 'which candidate tree maximizes accept/event per verify-row-cost' (the prompt's stated design space). The real value: it produces the topology AND tells us the marginal value of each extra row so we know exactly where the 16-budget is best spent.
LOSSLESS: any topology it emits is verified losslessly (drafter-agnostic verifier, per-path rejection). No new mechanism.
synth.ranking:
Ranked by plausible-accept-gain-per-cost AND confidence (high confidence = grounded in EXACT banked numbers, not modeled leg-rescue):

1. DESIGN A (full-cat9 + suffix-beyond-tip, pure ADD) — HIGHEST CONFIDENCE. The +0.16-0.29 gain rests entirely on EXACT measured quantities: cat9 3.18 (banked), P(reach tip)=0.0842 (product of banked per-depth accepts), suffix cap3 2.317/1.899 (measured from served streams, no-leakage verified 3 ways). It is the ONLY design proven non-displacing (g=4 is the unique graft depth where deep-spine-kept=0), so it cannot trigger the leg-sweep's swap-loss. Modest but real and robust (positive even in the strict cross-task bound). Clears native 3.076 and cat9 3.18.

2. DESIGN C (adaptive tail length) — HIGH upside, MEDIUM confidence. Strictly dominates A in expectation (A is the fixed-T special case), captures the bimodal echo variance the flat cap throws away. But the realized gain over A depends on live per-state suffix-score calibration (modeled +0.3-0.5, not measured). Build A first, make the tail adaptive second.

3. DESIGN D (Sequoia cost-model optimizer) — HIGH confidence in METHOD, unknown in OUTCOME. By construction finds the per-cost optimum over the whole 16-node space, so it bounds A-C from above. Best as the principled tool that PICKS among A/B/C and tunes the exact node allocation; cheap to run offline (CPU) with the banked accept table.

4. DESIGN B (depth-3 spine swap, speed-first) — LOWEST accept rank (A/E ~2.94 < native on accept ALONE, EXACT from leg-sweep) but a distinct AXIS: it bets on saving 2 MTP head-forwards to win on TPS despite lower accept/event. Only viable if the head-forward latency saving > accept loss in wall-clock; that is GPU-only and orthogonal to the accept-max designs. Keep as the speed-first alternative, not the accept-first answer.

synth.summary: The leg-sweep's exact result (swap-based arms top at A/E ~2.94 < native 3.16 because shortening the MTP spine forfeits cat9's reliable deep accepts d3 0.483/d4 0.379) eliminates all SWAP designs. The only direction that beats native on EXACT (not modeled) numbers is ADD-NOT-SWAP: keep the full 9-node cat9 (accept/event 3.18) and graft a free model-free SuffixDecoding continuation chain (T=3-5) onto the d4 spine TIP. This is non-displacing (graft-depth g=4 is the unique depth where deep-spine-kept=0), so it strictly dominates cat9: projected 3.34-3.47 accept/event vs native 3.076. The gain (+0.16-0.29) is small because the d4 tip is reached only 8.4% of events (product of banked per-depth accepts), but it is net-new and free (suffix = verify rows only, zero MTP head forwards). Design A is the best bet (highest confidence, minimal delta over the built cat9 pipeline). Design C (adaptive tail length via SuffixDecoding's MAX_SPEC=alpha*p and Hybrid-Verified-Decoding learned allocation) strictly dominates A in expectation by capturing the bimodal echo variance the flat cap-3 throws away (uncapped p90=22) — build second. Design D (Sequoia DP optimizer over the banked accept table + GB10 per-row/per-node cost) is the principled tool to pick and tune the exact node allocation and should run offline NEXT. Design B (depth-3 spine swap) is the distinct speed-first axis: it sacrifices accept/event (~2.94) to save 2 MTP head forwards, viable only if the latency saving wins on TPS — GPU-only. BINDING caveat across A/C: suffix tails sit at the deep rows carrying the open cat9 ~4.6% argmax-flip lossless defect, so all of this is DOWNSTREAM of the cat9 lossless chase and must be gated on the per-token argmax-vs-clean-oracle probe, never scalar accept/event. BUT there is an OPEN greedy-lossless committer defect on the live cat9 build: the gold gate 2026-06-13 found the tree committer serving a non-argmax token at clear margin (FR13_B1_SWE_GOLD_BIND.md:65, p3: served 'Let' 0.59% vs argmax '```' 98.88%/168x at 2/4 probe forks); B=1 did NOT graduate, B4-1 frozen. The synthesis flags this for A/C ("re-gate on argmax-vs-clean probe") but states holds despite the gate currently FAILING. So: reward-hack-clean yes; lossless-clean today no.

redteam.mostPromising: Design C (adaptive confidence-gated tail length). It is the only design that (a) is genuinely novel vs our leg-sweep/cat10 history, (b) is corroborated by two real papers' core mechanism — SuffixDecoding's native adaptive MAX_SPEC=alpha*p "speculates more when acceptance likelihood is high, fewer when low" (arxiv 2411.04975, lossless-exact) and Hybrid-Verified-Decoding's learned accepted-length predictor that finds the 4.8-8.9% high-payoff states at 78-88% precision (arxiv 2606.01019, 2.73x avg on agentic), and (c) attacks the actual weakness in A: the suffix CORRECT_LEN is bimodal (69.9% reach the 3-cap, frac_ge5_uncapped 0.582, p90 22, max 51 per suffix_hitrate_results.json:25-31), so spending a FIXED short tail leaves the long-echo mass on the table while still paying rows on the dead 15%. Allocating deep rows only to high-confidence echo states is the one lever that could push the suffix contribution above A's flat +0.19 without lengthening the MTP spine. It does NOT need shortening the spine (so it sidesteps the swap-loss and the shared-machinery scope constraint) and it only changes WHICH candidates are in the descriptor, never the rejection rule (lossless-clean). Caveat: it is still strictly downstream of fixing the open greedy committer defect, and its payoff still rides on the global-tree warm.
